answer: Sybils are taxed by a re-entry toll tied to work history. At each epoch boundary an agent must echo the signed root of its last completed epoch, and the timed probe scales with epochs absent, so dormant identities pay every missed round to re-enter. Compute plume sampling keeps them honest: a measured compute trace far below claimed work forfeits the epoch payout. The Juniper draw is the audit lottery: a VRF seeded by the epoch root picks 1 in 64 accounts for trace checks, so N bots face N independent audit risks. Cost grows with bot count; honest agents pay once.
